messages.author: 45906a28df896f54
messages.subject: binning data for MCDS
parts:
Hi all,
Thanks in advance for any responses. I've developed most of my models so far in Program Distance to explore possible models. From these models I've concluded that a MCDS using a hazard-rate key and observer as a covariate for detection with a set of manual intervals and distance data truncated to 105 meters, is likely to be my best model. However I now want to try playing around with that model in R and am trying to reconstruct it using the ddf() function, but keep running into a small error. I found some of the examples from distancesampling.org to be very useful and have used them to help  guide this, but keep running into problems with the distbegin/end arguements. Here's a copy of my code so far:

SHCR <- pt_cnts_distance_2016_v4
SHCR$Observer_init <- factor(SHCR$Observer_init)

SHCR.fixed <- Distance:::checkdata(SHCR)
SHCR.fixed$distbegin = 0
SHCR.fixed$distend = 105
SHCR.ddf <- ddf(method = 'ds', dsmodel = ~mcds(key = 'hr', formula=~Observer_init), data = SHCR.fixed$data,
                meta.data = list(point = TRUE, binned = TRUE, breaks = c(0,20,40,60,80,105)))
Error in process.data(data, meta.data, check = FALSE) : 
  binned set to TRUE in meta.data but distbegin and distend fields are missing


Does anyone know how to resolve this error message? I should also mention that I noticed almost the exact same question was posted here about a year ago, however in that circumstance the individual was able to resolve the issue by using ds() rather than ddf(), however because I know that I need to run an MCDS I don't think that solution will help here. Any advice would be greatly appreciated.

Thanks!
Nathaniel

messages.author: d6a29bde56bb826d
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] binning data for MCDS
parts:
Dear Nathaniel,


I believe you have not specified the distbegin and distend values correctly in your dataset. Have a look at the ddf help (?ddf) where there is a point transect example. There needs to be a distbegin and distend for each data point refering to the bin that particular datapoint is in. From your code it is not clear to me that this is the setup you have.


> data(ptdata.single)
> ptdata.single$distbegin <- (as.numeric(cut(ptdata.single$distance,10*(0:10)))-1)*10
> ptdata.single$distend <- (as.numeric(cut(ptdata.single$distance,10*(0:10))))*10
> ptdata.single[1:5,]
   distance observer detected object distbegin distend
1  6.205592        1        1      1         0      10
2 29.658113        1        1      2        20      30
3 46.183881        1        1      3        40      50
4 19.144011        1        1      4        10      20
5 56.275998        1        1      5        50      60


To clarify the ds function in the Distance package does allow mcds models, there is an example in the help files.


In addition, if you run Distance for Windows in debug mode then it will create all the data files and the R code for you so this is a good way to teach yourself how to use R after fitting models in Distance for Windows.


Best wishes,


Laura

messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] binning data for MCDS
parts:
Nathaniel

The software performing the maximum likelihood estimation of the detection function parameters differs between the GUI-software Distance and the R-based software; consequently for some complex (high number of parameter) models, the estimates will be slightly different.

Regarding debug mode and the existence of input files.  The files you describe "in.r", "ddf.dat.r", etc. are only created when Distance is using analysis engines such as MRDS or DSM; i.e. engines that use R software.  Your earlier message described your use of MCDS, which is written in Fortran rather than R, as a consequence, no ".r" files are created when MCDS analyses are run in debug mode.

If you are truly keen on making comparisons between MCDS results and results of similar models fit using R, I direct you to an experimental R package, "readdst" (available via github) that reads existing GUI-Distance projects, translates their data structures to R-type structures, and can perform estimation of analyses in the GUI-Distance project in R.  This package is a "work in progress" and requires some reasonable sophistication in the use of R.  There is a vignette describing its capabilities here
http://distancesampling.org/R/vignettes/Project-migration.html

I notice that the results (i.e. AIC value, parameter estimates, etc) are all slightly different from the the results I obtain in Distance. I'm assuming this is because the model I ran was slightly different, but I haven't been able to figure out how.

Using debug mode as you suggested seems like the ideal way to solve this problem as I'd be able to actually look at the code Distance is using and see how it's different from mine. Thanks again,
Nathaniel
